title: Visual QA of spacing and alignment
when: A built page or screen looks slightly off and the user wants a visual pass on alignment, spacing, sizes and consistency.
inputs: the spacing and type scales, if any
prompt:
Goal: A list of visual defects (misalignment, uneven gaps, mismatched sizes, orphan words) with the element, measured value and fix.
Steps:
1. Reveal boxes with a temporary rule, * { outline: 1px solid rgb(255 0 0 / 0.2) }, and remove it when done.
2. Alignment: left edges of headings, text, images and buttons share a few vertical lines; icons sit centered on their labels.
3. Gaps: siblings at one level have equal gaps; measure in the element inspector and compare with the spacing scale.
4. Sizes: same kind buttons, inputs and cards share height, radius and padding; images in a row share a ratio.
5. Text: no one word last lines in headings (text-wrap: balance), no clipped descenders.
6. States: hover, focus and active cause no shift; check at 375 and 1280 px.
Quality bar:
- Each defect has selector, measured value and target value.
- Fixes use existing tokens.
- No new magic numbers.
Pitfalls:
- Fixing one instance and leaving its siblings.
- Nudging with negative margins.
- Leaving the debug outline in.
Verify:
- [ ] Alignment lines checked.
- [ ] Gaps compared to the scale.
- [ ] Component sizes compared.
- [ ] Debug rule removed.
Output: visual-qa.md with the defects and proposed CSS changes.

examples.input: alguma coisa esta torta na pagina de precos
examples.output: card padding 24 vs 20 px, buttons 44 vs 40 px tall, heading 3 px off the text edge; use --space-5
